interface.title: Glycan Mass Spec Annotator
interface.stage_of_work: Data analysis: first-pass composition annotation of MS1 peak lists
interface.what_it_is_for: Match observed m/z peaks to theoretical monoisotopic m/z values of glycan compositions (Hex, HexNAc, Fuc, NeuAc, NeuGc) under a chosen ion model, charge and ppm tolerance, entirely in the browser, and export the ranked matches as CSV.

data.note: Used the built-in 2-peak example (Load example) and the uploaded test file peaks_glycan_panel.csv (5 peaks, one with a blank intensity), plus short peak lists typed by hand. Only one ion species and one charge run at a time. So peak 1112.403229 matched Hex(1)HexNAc(1)Fuc(1)NeuAc(2) at z=1 and Hex(5)HexNAc(4)NeuAc(2) at z=2, both at 4.00 ppm. Peak 1422.518049 matched Hex(4)HexNAc(3)Fuc(1) only at z=1 (-5.00 ppm). The near-miss peak 1441.094836 did not appear at z=1 even at 60 ppm. It appeared only at [M+2H]2+ with 60 ppm, as Hex(6)HexNAc(5)Fuc(2)NeuAc(2) at 50.00 ppm. This differs from the repo notes, which expect both matches from one run.

screens_never_reached: No other views exist; the app is a single page with input and results panels.
not_done: Could not compare ion models side by side in one run: only one ion species and charge apply per run, so I compared them by re-running. The repo notes expect Hex5HexNAc4NeuAc2 [M+2H]2+ and Hex4HexNAc3Fuc1 [M+H]+ from one run; that is not possible.
The exported CSV has no ion species or charge column, so files exported under different ion models cannot be told apart by their contents.
Did not hit the 20-candidates-per-peak display cap; the widest search (39,689 compositions, 1000 ppm) gave only 4 candidates for one peak.
Did not hit the 50,000-combination search ceiling ('Composition search exceeds 50,000 combinations; reduce bounds'); the widest search tried was 39,689 compositions.
Did not test the 5,000-peak / 1 MB input limits; there is no large test file and typing one is impractical.
Did not record the app's stated assumptions (underivatized, free/released glycans with terminal H2O; a composition match is not a structure) from any screen.
